Three parts.No glue code.

Every workflow is a trigger and a list of steps. That's the whole model, so there's nothing hidden to debug.

  1. 01 · Trigger

    Something happens

    A service calls your private webhook URL, a schedule comes due, or you press Run with some test data.

  2. 02 · Steps

    Knotwork does the work

    Call an API, reshape the data, skip what you don't need, wait, or write a note. Each step reads what came before.

  3. 03 · Run log

    You see every move

    Each run lists every attempt with its output and timing, updating live while it runs.

When things break

It fails.It waits.It holds.

APIs time out and rate-limit. Knotwork treats that as normal: a failed step waits a little longer each time, then tries again. A run saves its place after every step, so nothing starts over.

Five building blocks.That's the whole toolbox.

http

Call any API, pass the answer along

POST https://api.example.com/messages
{ "text": "New order trigger.body.id" }
// later steps read it as steps.post.body
transform

Reshape data

Build exactly the object the next step needs, with templates. Nothing is evaluated as code.

filter

Stop early

Carry on only when a condition holds, like an amount over 100.

delay

Wait

Pause for seconds or up to a week, then pick up where it left off.

log

Leave a note

Write a line into the run's history for whoever reads it next.
